Evan —

Thanks for the profile and the clear SLO. I ran a quick sizing pass with our assumptions and attached a concise workbook (novus_dedicated_sizing_calc.xlsx). TL;DR recommendation below so Procurement has something short for the MSA.

Assumptions (pilot):
- Model: rw-13B-q4f16 (production-equivalent variant we use for early pilots)
- Typical response length: 80 tokens
- Average tokens per user-turn: 220 (includes context + response)
- Steady-state target: 8,000 tokens/sec
- Peak bursts: 20,000 tokens/sec for up to 5 minutes, 2x/day
- Latency SLO (95th): <= 250ms for end-to-end response generation (network + runtime)

Performance baseline (observed on Redwood A100-optimized pool):
- Single GPU (rw-13B-q4f16, steady mix) => ~1,100 tokens/sec sustained, median per-request generation ~120ms, 95th ~210ms at low load
- GPU degrade curve: latency increases non-linearly past ~80% utilization; throughput flattens as batching saturates

Sizing & headroom calc (conservative):
- Steady capacity: ceil(8,000 / 1,100) = 8 GPUs => provides ~8,800 tps raw
- Operational headroom: +25% => 10 GPUs (to absorb spikes, scheduling jitter, autoscaler latency)
- Burst buffer for 20k tps spikes: we suggest a burst slab of 10 additional GPUs available via reserved burst or shared regional pool. With 20 total GPUs you reach ~22,000 tps raw which covers the 20k spike with ~10% cushion.

SLO fit summary:
- 10-GPU steady pool + 10-GPU burst slab meets 95th <= 250ms in our tests under the token distributions you sent (we modeled batching and KV cache miss rates).
- If burst slab is not provisioned, 10 GPUs will handle ~8-10k tps; a 20k spike will push utilization to ~180% and we'd expect 95th latencies to exceed 500ms and queuing to occur.

Fallback behavior (automated):
- When slab exhausted, Smart routing will failover to hosted lower-cost variant (rw-7B-q4) with graceful fallback: 95th latency for fallback ~300-400ms but lower quality for longer replies. We can configure a per-route policy to avoid fallbacks for critical flows.

Operational notes:
- Autoscaler cooldowns: 90s for horizontal adds; recommend pre-warming burst slab 2 minutes before expected sends (we can add a webhook from Novus control plane).
- Caching: enable prefix cache for repeated system prompts to reduce steady token volume by ~8-12% depending on reuse.
- Observability: we'll provide per-route 95/99 latency dashboards and token-level cost breakdown.

Next steps I propose:
1) If Procurement signs off on the 10 + 10 slab, we'll produce a compact MSA annex with the capacity table and ramp schedule.
2) Run a short stress test (2 hours) during a low-risk window to validate tail latency with your exact traffic mix.
3) Add SOC2 evidence pack to the DocuSign MSA (we'll attach audit artifacts).

I've looped in Marissa for commercial sizing and Karthik for the ops/runbook. We'll follow up with numbers you can paste into Procurement.

- Olga
